chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever belittles a believer or despises him for his poverty and lack of means, God will make him known publicly on the Day of Resurrection, and then He will disgrace him.

key_terms.ذات اليد: Means/wealth (literally: what is in the hand)
key_terms.شهره: To make known publicly / to expose

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of belittling a poor believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the spiritual gravity of *istidhla'* (humiliating) a believer, specifically targeting the common social vice of judging worth by material status. It serves as a stern warning that divine disgrace (*shahr*) on the Day of Resurrection is the direct consequence of diminishing the dignity of the faithful, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) towards all believers regardless of their economic standing. This concept is deeply rooted in the Imams' teachings on social equity and the intrinsic value of the soul over worldly wealth.
